links.outcome: AUROC of MIMIC-IV-trained sepsis model on German local ICU data versus MIMIC-IV test set
links.effect: Continuous evaluation, 6-hour horizon: AUROC 0.67 (95% CI 0.66–0.68) on BerlinICU versus 0.84 (95% CI 0.83–0.85) on MIMIC-IV test set.
links.quote: Application of a temporal convolution network model to BerlinICU yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.66–0.68) for continuous evaluation with a 6-hour prediction horizon, compared to 0.84 (95% CI: 0.83–0.85) on the test set of MIMIC-IV.

links.outcome: Variation of performance metrics across evaluation strategies (fixed horizon, peak score, continuous) on the same model and data
links.effect: Same model and dataset gave different AUROCs by strategy; fixed horizon AUROC was 0.61 (0.60–0.62) versus about 0.67 for continuous; peak score similar to continuous; metrics improved with shorter horizons.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that the choice of evaluation strategy has a significant impact on the performance metrics of intensive care prediction models.

unlisted_practices: Choice of evaluation strategy (continuous vs fixed-horizon vs peak-score) and onset matching for sepsis prediction model evaluation

screen.reason: Evaluates how different evaluation/validation methodologies (fixed horizon vs continuous vs peak score) impact measured performance metrics during external/local validation of an ICU sepsis prediction model.
